verdict.rationale: Devin documents real execution isolation: each cloud session runs in its own VM, and the CLI's --sandbox flag enforces OS-level write and deny rules with optional network restriction. That is genuine sandbox isolation rather than a dry run. However, nothing documents separating test data from production data. The VPN feature (devin-docs-28) actually lets sessions reach internal databases, so keeping production data out of reach is left to the user. Missing for 10: documented isolation of test or staging data from production, environment-level guardrails against production access, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The --sandbox flag runs the CLI with OS-level isolation, enforcing writable paths and deny rules at the operating-system level and optionally restricting network traffic.
The cloud session gets its own VM with a shell, browser, and full repo access
Configure it once, and every session boots into that known-good state.
